description: Two-person team harmonizing NASA FIRMS MODIS (2000-) and VIIRS (2012-) active-fire detections into comparable series, with 90% intervals, and exploring them on a web app. Challenge: Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots.
summary: MODIS (2000-) and VIIRS (2012-) active-fire detections from NASA FIRMS are not directly comparable: the sensors differ in resolution and detection behavior, Aqua's overpass time drifts (13:36 to about 15:30 by 2026), and the S-NPP mission ended on 2026-11-02. Long fire records therefore break at sensor changes. Fire Globe builds two harmonized monthly series in one unit (detections, not burned area): an Aqua-equivalent series from 2003 with 90% intervals, and a VIIRS 375 m series from 2013. A web app lets anyone explore them for any area, compare sensors side by side, query the data in the browser and export maps, tables and video. Each series comes with validation figures and declared limits, so users can judge when the numbers are safe to use.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

- Globe: MODIS, VIIRS, both side by side (split compare) or the Harmonized series; monthly and daily steps; single detections when zoomed in.

- Area fire calendar: pick an area by place search, continent, GFED region, drawn box, current view or point plus radius; month x year calendar, anomaly against the median of the same month in the other years, 90% interval for the harmonized series; CSV and PNG export.

- Climatology: typical range (5-95%) of the 7-day total of fire detections for each day of the year, with the current year on top. Descriptive, not a forecast.

- Data explorer: column filters, no-code builder, read-only SQL on DuckDB-WASM, charts.

- Export: maps as PNG and time animations as video, in 16:9, 4:3, 1:1 and 9:16, up to 4K.

- Quick start page, accessibility menu, 28 interface languages, installable on phones.

HOW IT WORKS

Data: NASA FIRMS active-fire detections, MODIS Collection 6.1 (Terra, Aqua) and VIIRS 375 m (S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21). Unit: detections; FRP is not harmonized.

Harmonization in plain terms:

(1) Static sources (volcano, other static, offshore) are masked with one rule for all sensors; the FIRMS type field is not trusted for this.

(2) VIIRS detections of one overpass in a ~1 km cell are clustered; each cluster weighs F^2 / (F^2 + 10^2), with F = summed FRP in MW, to mimic what a 1 km MODIS pixel detects. The daily VIIRS value is the mean of the satellites not in outage; NOAA-21 is scaled to NOAA-20.

(3) VIIRS is converted to Aqua units with a ratio per 2.5 degree block x calendar month x day/night, shrunk toward the latitude band, plus a 1 degree cell term.

(4) Calibration uses S-NPP against Aqua in 2013-2020, before Aqua's orbit drifted (overpass from 13:36 to about 15:30 by 2026). Nothing is recalibrated after 2020.

(5) Series "long": Aqua as observed up to 2021-12, then VIIRS converted to Aqua units, so 2022-2026 stay comparable with 2003-2021. Series "detail": VIIRS 375 m at S-NPP level from 2013; its band is the spread between satellites, not a confidence interval.

Uncertainty: 90% intervals from out-of-sample residuals (each year of 2013-2020 predicted from the other seven), with a drift term after 2020.

Validation (out of sample, re-runnable from the public data with data_pipeline/validation/make_validation.py): median annual difference from Aqua 1.7% per GFED region and 0.3% for the world (leave-one-year-out 2013-2020); 4.3% and 2.0% (calibrated 2013-2020, tested 2021-2025 against Aqua as observed, which drifts); 11% and 13% on single 1 degree cells; world step at the 2022 sensor seam +0.1%; coverage of the 90% intervals 88-93% across GFED regions, countries, continents and the world.

Architecture: a static site (GitHub Pages, no server, no login). A GitHub Action runs every night: it downloads the current year from the FIRMS API, applies the frozen harmonization and publishes. In the browser, DuckDB-WASM queries Parquet files with HTTP range requests; worldwide single detections of past years (about 6.6 GB) are a public Hugging Face dataset read the same way. Web app: Vite, TypeScript, CesiumJS.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Researchers get comparable multi-sensor series with intervals and re-runnable validation; journalists and the public can explore any area and export images and video; civil protection and agencies get regional totals, anomalies and the typical range for this time of year. The harmonized layer is meant for regional totals and trends, not for small single areas.

Local example: Sicily, July 2023 - vegetation fires across the island (3,337 VIIRS NOAA-20 detections in the month) and, kept as separate layers instead of discarded, the Etna and Stromboli volcanoes, industrial sites such as Priolo-Augusta and offshore flares.

CREATIVITY AND FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Detections that are usually thrown away as noise (volcanoes, industry, offshore flares) stay browsable as their own layers.

- Two series with different purposes instead of one compromise; uncertainty is shown wherever a harmonized number is shown.

- Nothing is invented before 2012: the long series stays Aqua as observed where Aqua is reliable.

- Built for everyone: no server, no account, nightly updates, accessibility menu (reduced motion, high contrast, colour-blind safe palette, larger text, keyboard navigation, text description and read aloud), 28 interface languages (25 machine-translated and declared as such), installable on phones.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES AND HARDWARE

TypeScript and Python; CesiumJS, DuckDB and DuckDB-WASM, Vite, Tabulator, Chart.js, CodeMirror, html-to-image; numpy, pandas, pyarrow, matplotlib. GitHub Pages, GitHub Actions, Hugging Face datasets. Developed and run on one laptop: Acer Nitro V 17 AI (AMD Ryzen 7 260, 32 GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Laptop GPU, 1 TB SSD, Windows 11).

LIMITS WE STATE OPENLY

- Values live on 1 degree cells: a small area counts every cell it overlaps, whole; use regional totals.

- Small fires get less weight in the Aqua-equivalent series; regional trends can differ in sign (Middle East, Europe); the detail series keeps them.

- No harmonized series before 2003; counts only, not burned area.

- After 2021 the checks are partly circular and the drift term is an assumption; 2026 data are partly near-real-time; S-NPP ended on 2026-11-02 and that seam rests on few days of data.
